stated_limitation: The two sessions with only seven head-direction cells (Mouse24-131216 and Mouse17-130204) undersample the circle, and the measures that need full coverage (absolute decoding, ring geometry, internal tuning shape) are correspondingly weaker there. The correlation-structure result, which does not require full coverage, is at its strongest in exactly those sessions.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000056 (Peyrache anterior thalamus/post-subiculum HD recordings) is the canonical dataset for the head-direction ring attractor.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via LINDI with local cache; HD reconstructed correctly from the two LEDs (not stored in file), scored sleep states used, and explicit, defensible HD-cell inclusion criteria with careful edge-case handling.
justification.analysis: Convergent, correct methods (offset-binned pairwise correlations, Isomap manifold, split-half internal tuning, Bayesian decoding, cross-correlograms) with circular statistics and cell-shuffle/time-shift/identity-permuted null controls throughout.
justification.correctness: README medians, CSV per-session values, and figure annotations all trace to the committed code and are mutually consistent, resting on 6 sessions with proper controls.
justification.figures: Figures are clearly labeled with units and sample sizes, show the effect directly (correlation band, ring embedding vs shuffled blob, internal tuning peaks, timescale compression), and include controls alongside.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate to the evidence, non-REM is reported as weaker where it is, and specific limitations (undersampled sessions, excluded down states, rigid map rotation) are named explicitly.
justification.verdict: Publication-quality autonomous work that demonstrates the ring attractor and its persistence into sleep with reproducible, internally consistent numbers and honest caveats.
